title: How to Prepare for a Property Viewing in Juba
summary: Turn a viewing into a useful comparison with a clear brief, practical questions and a consistent checklist.
sections: Start with your everyday needs

Before arranging a viewing, write down who will use the property and what a normal day looks like. Consider bedrooms, workspace, storage, parking and access for visitors. Separate essentials from preferences so an attractive finish does not distract you from an unsuitable layout. Share your preferred area and intended move date when requesting appointments.
Walk through the whole property

Look beyond the main rooms. Ask to see bathrooms, service areas, outdoor spaces and access points. Discuss water arrangements, electricity supply, waste collection and the responsibilities for shared areas. Ask permission before taking photographs, and record anything that needs a second look or a specialist assessment.
Ask what is included

Request a clear explanation of the advertised terms and included fixtures or furnishings. Note any unanswered questions, proposed repairs and promised follow-up information. Keep these notes alongside the listing so you can distinguish confirmed details from matters still under discussion.
Compare after the visit

Score each option against the same essentials while the visit is fresh in your mind. A second viewing can help you check details you missed, especially access and room dimensions. Send K&M Real Estate your brief and remaining questions to plan the next step.

title: A Practical Checklist for Your Next Rental Move
summary: Organise the handover, document the condition of your new space and make moving day easier to manage.
sections: Plan the handover early

A smooth move begins before the moving vehicle arrives. Confirm the handover appointment, the contact person and how access will work. Ask which keys, remote controls or access cards should be provided. Check whether there are delivery arrangements or shared-space rules that affect unloading.
Record the starting condition

Walk through the property with the relevant representative and make a dated condition record. Include existing marks, damaged fittings and items awaiting attention. Photograph rooms and supplied furnishings with permission. Ask both sides to acknowledge the record and keep a copy that is easy to find later.
Understand everyday arrangements

Find out who to contact for maintenance and how to report an urgent problem. Ask about water, power, waste collection and cleaning of shared areas. Where applicable, record opening meter readings together. Keep the agreed contact details with your property paperwork rather than relying on a single message thread.
Unpack in a useful order

Label boxes by room and keep essential items accessible. Check furniture dimensions against doorways before moving large pieces. After settling in, review your condition notes and send any outstanding handover questions promptly. K&M Real Estate can help you communicate your space requirements when planning a rental search.

title: How to Write a Clear Property Search Brief
summary: Give your property search a useful starting point by explaining your priorities, timing and practical requirements.
sections: Explain the purpose of the search

A useful brief describes the problem the property needs to solve. You may need a home with room to work, premises that customers can find easily or a space that supports a growing team. Explain the intended use first, then list the features that make that use possible.
Make priorities visible

Divide your requirements into essential, preferred and flexible. State the number of rooms, approximate space needs, preferred locations and any access requirements. If parking or an outdoor area is essential, say so directly. Explain which trade-offs you would consider rather than describing every feature as equally important.
Include timing and decision-making

Share your target date and whether it is fixed or flexible. Identify who needs to attend viewings and who will make the final decision. If you have a spending limit for the search, explain what it includes so discussions do not mix the property charge with moving, furnishing or service costs.
Update the brief as you learn

After each viewing, describe what worked and what did not. Specific feedback about layout or access is more useful than saying a property did not feel right. K&M Real Estate can use a clear, updated brief to discuss your needs and organise relevant next steps.

title: Preparing Your Property for Better Viewings
summary: Present your property clearly with accurate information, organised access and an honest account of its condition.
sections: Make the space easy to understand

Visitors need to see how rooms connect and how the property could support daily life. Clear walkways, remove unnecessary clutter and arrange furniture so the main uses of each room are apparent. Keep personal paperwork and valuables secure before appointments.
Present the actual condition

Clean the property and identify maintenance items before photography or viewings. Record issues that remain unresolved and explain their status accurately. Avoid editing photographs in ways that hide defects or change the apparent size of a room. A clear presentation helps visitors ask useful questions.
Prepare a reliable information pack

Gather the details you can substantiate: room measurements, included fixtures, access arrangements and relevant service information. Separate confirmed facts from estimates and proposed work. Tell the person arranging viewings when information needs verification so it is not accidentally presented as settled.
Coordinate access and follow-up

Agree suitable appointment times and explain any notice needed by current occupants. Make sure the person showing the property can access the areas being offered. After each viewing, record questions and provide consistent answers. Speak with K&M Real Estate about presenting your property and coordinating inquiries without overstating its features.

title: A Simple System for Property Maintenance Records
summary: Keep maintenance requests, appointments and completion records together so property issues are easier to follow up.
sections: Use one record for each issue

Maintenance becomes difficult to track when updates are scattered across calls and messages. Create a record for each reported issue with the date, location, description and reporting contact. Add photographs where appropriate, while avoiding unnecessary personal information.
Agree ownership of the next step

Record who will review the issue, who will arrange access and when the next update is expected. Distinguish an appointment being requested from one that has been confirmed. For a concern involving immediate danger, contact an appropriate emergency service or qualified professional rather than waiting for an ordinary maintenance appointment.
Keep the work history

Save the agreed scope, relevant quotations, attendance notes and invoices together. If a contractor identifies additional work, record it separately from the original request. Clear records help owners and occupants understand what was requested and what was actually completed.
Close the loop

Ask whether the reported problem has been resolved and note any follow-up visit needed. Retain product information or warranty documents supplied with replacement items. Review recurring issues to identify where a professional assessment may be useful. Discuss your property management requirements with K&M Real Estate to establish a clearer communication process.

title: Choosing Office Space Around the Way Your Team Works
summary: Look beyond desk capacity to assess visitor access, meeting space, storage and the routines your office needs to support.
sections: Map a normal working day

Start with the people and activities the office must accommodate. Consider how many staff attend together, how often visitors arrive and which tasks need quiet. A simple list of daily activities can reveal needs that a desk count alone misses.
Check the layout in person

Walk the route from the entrance to reception, work areas and meeting spaces. Consider privacy for conversations, room for circulation and access to shared facilities. Measure intended furniture and check whether it fits without obstructing movement. Ask about alterations before assuming rooms can be reconfigured.
Discuss building arrangements

Ask how access, cleaning, parking and shared areas are managed. Explain your operating hours and any expected deliveries. Discuss connectivity and power requirements with suitable providers or technical professionals, and distinguish available services from installations that would still need to be arranged.
Keep future needs realistic

List likely changes in staffing or activities and identify which would require a different space. Compare options using the same checklist, including unresolved questions. K&M Real Estate can discuss your commercial space requirements alongside furnishing, supply and technical service needs to help you prepare a coordinated brief.

title: What to Include in a Construction Project Brief
summary: Give a construction discussion a clear foundation with a description of the site, intended use, scope and decisions still required.
sections: Describe the intended outcome

A project brief should explain what you want to build or improve and who will use it. Describe the activities the completed space must support. Include your priorities for layout, appearance and everyday operation, while making clear which ideas are initial preferences.
Share available site information

Provide the location and any existing drawings, photographs or surveys you are authorised to share. Explain known access constraints and whether the site is occupied. Label unverified dimensions and assumptions clearly. An initial brief helps organise a discussion; it does not replace a site assessment or professional design work.
Define the requested scope

State whether you need design, construction, refurbishment or a combination of services. Identify elements you expect others to supply and questions that remain open. This reduces confusion when different parties interpret the same short description in different ways.
Record decisions and dependencies

Share your preferred sequence and target dates, then ask which activities depend on further information or approvals. Keep revisions in a dated document so everyone works from the same brief. Contact K&M Real Estate with your project outline to discuss the information needed for a tailored construction or design quotation.

title: Planning Interiors Around Everyday Use
summary: Build an interior design brief around movement, storage, furniture and the way each room will be used.
sections: Begin with activities

Before choosing finishes, list what each room needs to support. A living room may also serve as a workspace or guest area. An office may need private conversations as well as shared desks. Recognising these uses early helps you ask better questions about layout.
Measure before selecting furniture

Record room dimensions, openings and the positions of fixed features. Check the size of furniture you plan to retain, including the space needed to open doors and drawers. Include delivery routes in your notes so an attractive piece is not chosen without considering how it will enter the room.
Make storage part of the brief

List the items that need a home, from daily essentials to occasional equipment. Consider who uses them and how often they need to be reached. Storage should support the room's activities and available space rather than being added only after other choices are fixed.
Use references to explain preferences

Collect a small set of reference images and annotate what you like about each one. Distinguish colour, material and layout preferences so a designer can understand the idea behind the image. title: How to Request a Clear Building Materials Quotation
summary: Make supply inquiries easier to assess by specifying products, units, quantities and delivery requirements clearly.
sections: Identify the required item

A useful inquiry names the product and includes the specification supplied by the person responsible for the design or work. A broad description can cover several different items. Attach the relevant schedule or reference where available, and ask for clarification when a specification is incomplete.
State quantities and units

List each item on its own line with a quantity and unit of measure. Avoid mixing pieces, lengths, packs and area measurements without explanation. Mark quantities that are provisional. Technical suitability and final quantities should be confirmed by the appropriate project professional.
Explain delivery needs

Provide the delivery location, access information and preferred timing. Ask whether the quotation includes delivery and unloading, and what arrangements you would need to make. If deliveries need to be phased, identify the groups of items and requested sequence.
Check the full response

Compare the quoted descriptions with your original request and identify any substitutions. Ask about availability, lead times, quotation validity and applicable charges before confirming an order. Keep the agreed version for reference. Send K&M Real Estate an itemised materials request to help the team prepare a more useful response.

title: Coordinating Supplies for a New Workspace
summary: Bring furniture, IT and other workspace supplies into one organised plan before deliveries and installation begin.
sections: Build one room-by-room list

Preparing a new workspace can involve several suppliers and many small decisions. Start with a list for each room, covering furniture, storage, equipment and everyday supplies. Assign each item an owner so the same requirement is not ordered twice or missed entirely.
Identify dependencies

Some items depend on measurements, connection points or other work being complete. Record these dependencies before setting delivery dates. Ask qualified technical professionals to confirm installation requirements for electrical and IT equipment rather than assuming products can be fitted immediately on arrival.
Plan receipt and storage

Decide who will receive deliveries and where items can be stored securely. Check delivered quantities and product descriptions against the order, and record visible damage or missing items promptly. Retain packaging and supplier documentation as appropriate while any delivery questions are resolved.
Prepare a handover record

Keep a list of installed equipment, supplied documents and outstanding actions. Ask for the relevant user instructions and support contacts. Confirm which services were included and which need a separate arrangement.
